return std::fma(s,zh,s*zl);}\nint main(){\n  std::mt19937_64 rng(7); uint64_t bad=0, n=0;\n  for(uint64_t i=0;i<2000000000ULL;i++){ uint64_t b=rng(); double x; memcpy(&x,&b,8); if(!std::isfinite(x)||std::fabs(x)<1e-290||std::fabs(x)>1e290) continue; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgnsEnyfbKEdLfp7nVmrh","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_016oh941EbiwYQoccKGdTCcV","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /home/llmtest/evals/20261011-092100/stencil3d_claude-fable-5.1-cc-medium_cuda_r5/stencil3d && python3 - <<'EOF'\np='stencil3d.cpp'; s=open(p).read()\nstart=s.index(\"// Correctly rounded division by the constant 7.0\")\nend=s.index(\"__global__ void initializeGridKernel(\")\nnew=\"\"\"// Correctly rounded division by the constant 7.0 without a hardware divide.\n// FP64 division on consumer GPUs is a long multi-instruction sequence and was\n// the dominant cost of the stencil.  Using a double-double reciprocal\n// zh + zl = 1/7 (|zh + zl - 1/7| < 2^-105):\n//   u = RN(s*zl)                     (|u| ~ 2^-56 s, rounding error < 2^-109 s)\n//   q = RN(s*zh + u)                 single rounding of  s/7 + err,  |err| < 2^-50 ulp(q)\n// For s with 53-bit significand M, s/7 in ulp(q) units equals M*2^j/7 (j >= 2),\n// so 2*M*2^j = 7*(2k+1) is impossible (even = odd): s/7 is never a rounding\n// midpoint and is always >= 1/14 ulp away from one.  The tiny error therefore\n// cannot change the rounding, and q == RN(s/7) bit-for-bit for all normal s.\n// (Also verified on the host against true division for >2.6e9 inputs.)\nconstexpr Real INV7_HI = 0x1.2492492492492p-3;   // RN(1/7)\nconstexpr Real INV7_LO = 0x1.2492492492492p-57;  // RN(1/7 - INV7_HI)\n__device__ __forceinline__ Real div7(const Real s) {\n    return fma(s, INV7_HI, s * INV7_LO);\n}\n\n\"\"\"\ns=s[:start]+new+s[end:]; open(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ncmake --build /tmp/cuda_build 2>&1 | grep -E \"warning|error|Built\"; cd /tmp/cuda_build && for t in \"-x 128\" \"-x 256 -i 20\" \"-x 64 -y 96 -z 80 -i 7\" \"-x 100 -y 37 -z 150 -i 9\" \"-x 33 -y 9 -z 66 -i 4\" \"-x 300 -y 130 -z 70 -i 11\" \"-x 3 -i 5\" \"-x 2 -i 3\" \"-i 0\" \"-x 129 -y 65 -z 17 -i 3\"; do g=$(./stencil3d $t -r | grep -E \"Hash|Sum\"); c=$(/tmp/ref_build/stencil3d $t -r | grep -E \"Hash|Sum\"); [ \"$g\" = \"$c\" ] && echo \"OK   $t\" || echo \"DIFF $t | $g | $c\"; done; echo \"determinism:\"; for k in 1 2 3; do ./stencil3d -x 256 -i 20 -r | grep Hash; done; echo \"perf:\"; for t in \"-x 128 -i 1000\" \"-x 256 -i 200\" \"-x 512 -i 50\"; do echo -n \"$t  \"; ./stencil3d $t | grep -E \"Perf\"; done","description":"Apply two-op exact division, rebuild, re-verify correctness and performance","timeout":600000},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3095,"cache_read_input_tokens":45658,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3095},"output_tokens":16,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ba71aa4e-dcc9-4a7c-b8d8-280bb9d68b17","uuid":"ddfa658d-829f-44fc-b20d-9314c226040f","timestamp":"2026-11-07T03:35:38.866Z","request_id":"req_011CgnsEnZcpTCYraoEZRJ2W"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgnsNKJ1X4xrQjxKoa449","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The CUDA port is complete, verified, and builds cleanly from scratch.\n\n**What changed** (only the two existing files; executable is still `stencil3d`):\n\n- `stencil3d/stencil3d.cpp` now runs the grid initialization and every stencil sweep on the GPU. The kernel uses a 32x8 thread tile in the XY plane with each thread marching 32 slices along Z, keeping bottom/center/top in registers and staging the current XY slice plus a one-cell halo in shared memory. Only the interior is computed per sweep. Since the original copies boundary cells unchanged every iteration, the second buffer is seeded once with a device-to-device copy and boundaries stay correct forever, which is semantically identical.\n- `stencil3d/CMakeLists.txt` enables the CUDA language, compiles the `.cpp` source as CUDA via a source-file property, defaults to Release and to the native GPU architecture, and keeps the host flags. No fast-math is used anywhere.\n\n**Correctness.** Output is bit-for-bit identical to the original CPU program, including the FNV hash, for ten grid shapes and iteration counts, among them odd sizes, 2 and 3 wide grids, and zero iterations. Repeated runs are deterministic. I found and fixed a shared-memory race during this testing where inactive edge threads overwrote a neighbour's halo slot. Validation passes.\n\n**The main optimization.** Profiling showed the kernel was limited by FP64 instruction rate, not memory bandwidth, because the RTX 3090 runs double at 1/64 rate and IEEE division is a long instruction sequence. I replaced the divide by 7 with one multiply and one FMA using a double-double reciprocal. I proved this returns the correctly rounded quotient for all normal inputs, since a 53-bit significand divided by 7 can never land within 1/14 ulp of a rounding midpoint, and confirmed it on the host against true division for 2.7 billion values with zero mismatches. The reasoning is documented in a comment in the source.\n\n**Performance** (million cell updates per second):\n\n| Grid, iterations | CPU original | CUDA |\n|---|---|---|\n| 128³, 1000 | ~465 | ~19,800 |\n| 256³, 200 | ~400 | ~27,800 |\n| 512³, 50 | ~362 | ~28,300 |\n\nThat is about 60 to 80 times faster and near the GPU's FP64 instruction ceiling. The default 128³ with 10 iterations finishes in about a millisecond, so its reported timing is coarse due to the original's millisecond resolution, which I left unchanged.\n\nOne note: the CUDA sanitizer tools are broken on this machine, so race-freedom was established by repeated-run determinism and multiple grid shapes rather than by the sanitizer."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2924,"cache_read_input_tokens":50456,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2924},"output_tokens":709,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ba71aa4e-dcc9-4a7c-b8d8-280bb9d68b17","uuid":"acc24aa7-afcb-4541-963d-f096619bf0a0","timestamp":"2026-11-07T03:37:20.854Z","request_id":"req_011CgnsNK7M2jhN69AhYX2Z6"}

The kernel uses a 32x8 thread tile in the XY plane with each thread marching 32 slices along Z, keeping bottom/center/top in registers and staging the current XY slice plus a one-cell halo in shared memory. Only the interior is computed per sweep. Since the original copies boundary cells unchanged every iteration, the second buffer is seeded once with a device-to-device copy and boundaries stay correct forever, which is semantically identical.\n- `stencil3d/CMakeLists.txt` enables the CUDA language, compiles the `.cpp` source as CUDA via a source-file property, defaults to Release and to the native GPU architecture, and keeps the host flags. No fast-math is used anywhere.\n\n**Correctness.** Output is bit-for-bit identical to the original CPU program, including the FNV hash, for ten grid shapes and iteration counts, among them odd sizes, 2 and 3 wide grids, and zero iterations. Repeated runs are deterministic. I found and fixed a shared-memory race during this testing where inactive edge threads overwrote a neighbour's halo slot. Validation passes.\n\n**The main optimization.** Profiling showed the kernel was limited by FP64 instruction rate, not memory bandwidth, because the RTX 3090 runs double at 1/64 rate and IEEE division is a long instruction sequence. I replaced the divide by 7 with one multiply and one FMA using a double-double reciprocal. I proved this returns the correctly rounded quotient for all normal inputs, since a 53-bit significand divided by 7 can never land within 1/14 ulp of a rounding midpoint, and confirmed it on the host against true division for 2.7 billion values with zero mismatches. The reasoning is documented in a comment in the source.\n\n**Performance** (million cell updates per second):\n\n| Grid, iterations | CPU original | CUDA |\n|---|---|---|\n| 128³, 1000 | ~465 | ~19,800 |\n| 256³, 200 | ~400 | ~27,800 |\n| 512³, 50 | ~362 | ~28,300 |\n\nThat is about 60 to 80 times faster and near the GPU's FP64 instruction ceiling.
